answer.rationale: Deferral is not viable because the primary contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew, and renewal/negotiation with the incumbent is unlikely to meet the mandated 18% cut after price reopening was refused. The only credible cost lever is moving primary volume toward the previously low-cost vendor, but at 94% committed volume and no buffer this must be treated as a guarded cutover rather than a clean broad switch. I want to verify the low-cost switch outcome and the incumbent-stability record before committing, because those two memories most directly determine whether savings are real and what delivery/integration risk is being given up.
